article_title: Our DNA dilemma: Why we broke the law to make sure we were not siblings

tasks.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
options: A donor-conceived French couple's struggle to confirm they were unrelated and to gain access to their biological origins
A French programme encouraging all couples to use commercial DNA tests
A court case that ended anonymous sperm donation throughout Europe in 1994
A medical study proving that donor-conceived people usually marry relatives
tasks.correct_answer: A donor-conceived French couple's struggle to confirm they were unrelated and to gain access to their biological origins
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה עוסקת במאבקם האישי והמשפטי של אודרי וארתור לדעת שאינם קרובי משפחה ולגלות את מוצאם הביולוגי.

tasks.prompt: Why did Audrey and Arthur believe there was a real possibility they might be half-siblings?
options: They had the same legal surname
Only two sperm banks operated in Paris when they were conceived, and donors could donate many times
A court told them they shared the same donor
Their parents had lived in the same house
tasks.correct_answer: Only two sperm banks operated in Paris when they were conceived, and donors could donate many times
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מספר בנקי הזרע המצומצם וריבוי התרומות של אותם גברים יצרו אפשרות ממשית לתורם משותף.

tasks.prompt: What did the group DNA test reveal about the 10 donor-conceived activists?
options: None of them had any genetic matches
All 10 shared one biological father
Four of them were linked to the same donor
Only Arthur discovered a biological sibling
tasks.correct_answer: Four of them were linked to the same donor
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מבין עשרת הפעילים, ארבעה — אודרי, פיטר, סופי ודיוויד — התבררו כילדיו של אותו תורם.

tasks.prompt: Why did the first doctor's €900 test fail to remove the couple's anxiety completely?
options: The result said they were definitely siblings
The doctor refused to conduct any genetic analysis
The test only examined Audrey's medical history
Because the doctor acted illegally, they doubted whether he and the result were trustworthy
tasks.correct_answer: Because the doctor acted illegally, they doubted whether he and the result were trustworthy
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מאחר שהבדיקה בוצעה ושווקה בניגוד לחוק, בני הזוג חששו שהרופא שרלטן ולא בטחו לגמרי בתוצאה.

tasks.prompt: What does “a leap of faith” mean when the couple decided to marry?
options: A decision made with trust despite unresolved uncertainty
A legal order requiring them to marry
A scientific method for comparing two DNA samples
A public ceremony supporting donor anonymity
tasks.correct_answer: A decision made with trust despite unresolved uncertainty
tasks.explanation_hebrew: a leap of faith הוא צעד שנעשה מתוך אמון אף שאין ודאות מלאה — כאן, הנישואים לפני פתרון סופי של הספק.

tasks.prompt: What does “charlatan” mean when Audrey worried about the doctor?
options: A judge who specialises in medical law
A relative discovered through genetic testing
A dishonest person pretending to have professional knowledge or skill
A donor who asks to remain anonymous
tasks.correct_answer: A dishonest person pretending to have professional knowledge or skill
tasks.explanation_hebrew: charlatan הוא אדם שמתחזה לבעל מומחיות מקצועית כדי להטעות אחרים.

tasks.prompt: Construct a brief timeline of at least five key events in Audrey and Arthur's search for certainty and their biological origins.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לסדר לפחות חמישה אירועים לפי הרצף הכרונולוגי ולציין שנים כאשר הן מופיעות בכתבה.
expected_points: They met at a gathering of donor-conceived activists in 2010
A doctor in southern France tested them illegally and said they were unrelated
Audrey began legal challenges to the French system in 2010
They married after three years of challenges, in 2013
France's highest administrative court rejected Audrey's final appeal in 2015
Another doctor learned that their donors were born in different years
They eventually took a home DNA test confirming they were unrelated
Arthur contacted his sperm donor on Christmas Day in 2017
Audrey discovered that Sophie, a former client, was her biological sister
A later match led Audrey to her deceased donor, Philippe

tasks.prompt: Present the strongest argument for France's home-DNA-test ban and the strongest criticism raised by the couple's experience.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג באופן מאוזן טיעון בעד החוק וטיעון נגדו, ולבסס כל צד בפרטים מן הכתבה.
expected_points: Supporters say the ban protects sensitive genetic data from commercial companies
Supporters say it can prevent family disputes caused by unexpected results
Genetic tests are limited to authorised scientific, medical or judicial settings
Critics argue the ban denies people practical access to information about their origins
The couple could not obtain information needed to assess whether they were related
Doctors could see donor information that patients themselves could not receive
More than a million French people are estimated to have taken tests despite the ban
Testing exposed genuine shared-donor relationships among the activists
People may gain useful biological family medical history through matches

tasks.prompt: Summarise the couple's dilemma, the legal obstacles, what DNA testing revealed and the law's later change.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את החשש לקרבה משפחתית, מגבלות החוק, התגליות האישיות והיקף הרפורמה המאוחרת.
expected_points: Audrey and Arthur were both conceived through anonymous sperm donation
They feared they might share a donor because of the small number of Paris sperm banks
French law restricts genetic testing and criminalises home DNA tests
An illegal doctor-led test and later donor birth-year information suggested they were unrelated
After unsuccessful legal challenges, they used a home DNA test
The test confirmed they were not related
Arthur found his donor and Audrey found biological siblings and later identified her donor
Four of 10 activists tested shared the same donor
Their campaigning contributed to changes in donor-conception law
People conceived after April 2025 may access identifying donor information as adults
Home DNA testing nevertheless remains prohibited in France

tasks.prompt: Write a policy recommendation for France on donor information and home DNA testing. Use evidence from the article and address privacy as well as the right to know one's origins.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע מדיניות מאוזנת באנגלית, להשתמש לפחות בשלוש ראיות מן הכתבה ולהתייחס הן לפרטיות והן לגישה למידע.
expected_points: Protect genetic data through clear consent and security requirements
Offer a regulated testing route rather than leaving people to illegal providers
Allow donor-conceived adults access to identifying or relevant non-identifying information
Provide counselling before and after unexpected genetic discoveries
Set rules for contacting donors and newly discovered relatives
Include medical-history access where appropriate
Recognise the risk that people from a small donor pool may unknowingly be related
Learn from evidence that many people bypass the existing ban
Preserve safeguards against commercial misuse
Apply reforms fairly to people conceived before as well as after April 2025
